title: Hardware: the valve ignores its command
summary: The cabinet was wired and the PLC is in RUN. After Start the program commands the inlet valve, but the tank does not fill. Follow the output from the PLC to the valve.
objectives: Follow an output from the program to the actuator
Distinguish a commanded output from a switched terminal
starterProgram:
PROGRAM Main
VAR_INPUT
    StartPB : BOOL; (* Start button S1, normally open. *)
    StopPB : BOOL; (* Stop button S2, normally closed: TRUE while not pressed. *)
    LevelHigh : BOOL; (* High level switch LSH-305: TRUE when wet. *)
    InletOpen : BOOL; (* Inlet valve XV-301 open limit switch. *)
    InletClosed : BOOL; (* Inlet valve XV-301 closed limit switch. *)
    LevelRaw : INT; (* LT-303, 4-20 mA, 2-wire: generic profile 0..10000 = 0..100 %. *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    InletValve : BOOL; (* Inlet valve XV-301 solenoid. *)
    RunLamp : BOOL; (* Green lamp H1: filling with the inlet valve open. *)
    FaultLamp : BOOL; (* Red lamp H2: level invalid or high level. *)
    LevelOut : INT; (* Level retransmitted to the control room, 0..10000 = 0..100 %. *)
    LevelPercent : REAL; (* Level from LT-303, 0..100 %. *)
END_VAR
VAR
    LevelValid : BOOL; (* The level measurement is plausible: above 2 % and within range. *)
    Filling : BOOL; (* Fill request latch. *)
END_VAR
(* The program passed its factory test; this lab is about the station hardware. *)
LevelPercent := INT_TO_REAL(LevelRaw) / 100.0;
LevelValid := (LevelRaw > 200) AND (LevelRaw <= 10000);
(* Filling starts only from the valve's start position (closed and confirmed). *)
Filling := ((StartPB AND InletClosed) OR Filling) AND StopPB AND NOT LevelHigh AND LevelValid AND LevelPercent < 80.0;
InletValve := Filling;
RunLamp := Filling AND InletOpen;
FaultLamp := NOT LevelValid OR LevelHigh;
LevelOut := LevelRaw;
END_PROGRAM
instructions: The PLC runs the accepted program. Let the simulation run, press Start and confirm the symptom.
Open the Hardware tab: compare the configured (project) station with the detected one, then follow the signals.
Select a module for its channels, power and diagnostics; measure terminals with the multimeter.
Diagnose, repair (configuration labs: correct the configuration in Advanced mode and download it), then verify.
hints: Follow the signal: PLC output, module, terminal voltage, valve.
The module's status and the terminal voltage tell different parts of the story.

scenarios.title: Start filling and reach the setpoint

criteria.title: The level measurement agrees with the tank
criteria.onFail: LevelPercent was not about 20 % while the tank held 20 %.

criteria.title: The run lamp shows filling with the valve open
criteria.onFail: The run lamp never lit: filling and an open inlet valve are both needed.

troubleshooting.symptom: The tank does not fill. The PLC shows the inlet valve commanded, but the valve stays closed and the run lamp stays dark.

diagnosisOptions.label: The output module has no 24 V field (load) supply
The output module's electronics are not supplied, so the module does not answer
The module in slot 4 is not the type the project configures
The analog input module is mounted in another slot than configured
The valve's closed limit switch is wired to another input terminal
The level transmitter's channel is configured for the wrong signal type
The level transmitter LT-303 is defective
The inlet valve solenoid is defective

repairs.label: Replace the blown fuse in the output module's 24 V load supply
Replace LT-303 with a new transmitter

debrief.rootCause: The output module's 24 V field (load) supply was missing because its fuse had blown. The module electronics worked and answered the CPU, so the PLC set InletValve and the module accepted the command, but without load voltage no current could reach the valve solenoid.
evidence: InletValve was TRUE in the PLC, but the output terminal measured 0 V.
The Hardware view showed the output module answering, with a field (load) supply finding and a flashing red status LED.
The valve's limit switches stayed at closed, so the valve never moved.
debrief.repair: Replace the fuse of the output module's 24 V load supply, then switch the outputs again and repeat the fill test.
debrief.reasoning: A commanded output is not a switched terminal. Follow the chain: PLC tag, module command, field supply, terminal voltage, actuator, feedback. The first link that is missing is where to look.
